selected.title: Regulator warns Australians about 'highly speculative' prediction markets
selected.summary: The Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) says it is not currently convinced that prediction markets for retail clients are in the public interest, warning that people who access offshore platforms do not have legal protections.
selected.why: ASIC signals skepticism on retail prediction markets, effectively setting regulatory policy against offshore and domestic platforms.

reason: ASIC's prediction market warning assumes retail participation is inherently risky; the arguable position is that this paternalism blocks beneficial price-discovery mechanisms.
angle: Regulators should permit retail prediction markets because they improve information aggregation better than protecting people from speculative loss.
